category_title: Students with learning disabilities who manage fast-paced lectures by focusing on discrete information categories
minimal_context: Sandra is watching a 15-minute video lecture on Electro-Plasma Rockets and attempting to record notes on traditional note-taking paper.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to watch a 15-minute video lecture on Electro-Plasma Rockets. Please take notes on your regular note-taking paper.

STUDENT: Okay, I'll try to get the 3-6 main points and try to find some definitions.

TUTOR: I will start the video now. Just keep writing as you listen.

STUDENT: (Writing frantically) It's moving too fast. With regular notes I have to write down everything and then I read through it...

TUTOR: Just keep trying to write down what you hear.

STUDENT: I can't record it as fast as I'm hearing it! And some of the stuff I can't remember, 'cause it's too much. I'm completely lost and missing large chunks of the lecture.

options.A: Teach the student to modify or shift parts of the note-taking strategy based on changing lecture demands.
options.B: Provide individual storage space for the student, such as chair bags or desks with compartments, during the science lecture.
options.C: Assign brief reflective homework about the video lecture using Likert scales and two to three open-ended questions.
options.D: Teach the student to enter information into a tracking form, checking the appropriate box after the science lecture and turning it in for verification.
